newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares reach new record but need buy orders.
newsitem.headline: German shares reach new record but need buy orders.

text.p: German shares posted modest gains in pre-bourse IBIS computer dealings to reach a new all-time high on Wednesday at 3,844.65 points but traders said they wondered how long the market could stay at current levels.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade, was up 2.40 points at 3,837.24 points and well above the DAX's close of bourse on Tuesday at 3,819.85 points.

"We have to see whether some fresh buy orders show up this morning. The volumes have been relatively thin," said one Frankfurt trader. "If we don't see some new action, the market is certainly going to come under some pressure."
Gains may also be limited due to cautious trading ahead of the Federal Reserve releasing the results of its FOMC policy meeting later on Wednesday.
The IBIS DAX in late afternoon dealings on Tuesday surged toward all-time high levels, fuelled by gains on Wall Street and the dollar stabilising above 1.74 marks.

The German market has also found strength from investors taking a renewed interest in the chemical sector and Hoechst AG, which rose nearly six percent on buy recommendations from some brokerage houses.

"The chemicals are still in demand this morning but they are due for some consolidation after Tuesday," said a trader. "The uptrend, however, is still there and the shares have only just begun to climb."
Hoechst rose six pfennigs to 78.85 marks, while BASF was down two at 65.88 and Bayer was up 70 at 70.85.
Banking shares were also in the spotlight on Wednesday, in part due to the higher dollar, traders said.
Detusche Bank AG led the advance and reached a new all-time high at 105.15 marks in IBIS dealings. Deutsche shares were later up 1.65 marks at 104.65 marks.
Banking rivals Commerzbank AG and Dresdner Bank AG were also higher, with Commerzbank up 61 pfennigs at 49.89 marks and Dresdner up 23 pfennigs at 61.65 marks.
Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG were down 27 pfennigs at 42.35 marks after the telephone group said it had reached a deal with Kirch and CLT-Ufa over offering digital television in Germany.
